definition: In computer science, Universal IR Evaluation (information retrieval evaluation) aims to develop measures of database retrieval performance that shall be comparable across all information retrieval tasks.
details: In computer science, Universal IR Evaluation (information retrieval evaluation) aims to develop measures of database retrieval performance that shall be comparable across all information retrieval tasks.

explainer.lead: Universal IR evaluation aims to develop measures of database retrieval performance that are comparable across all information retrieval tasks. It matters because retrieval results are otherwise hard to compare between different tasks and settings.

tiers.eli5: It's about finding a single way to score search systems so you can fairly compare them no matter what they're searching.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers working on retrieval evaluation look for measures that hold up across tasks so results can be compared consistently. A pitfall is assuming a measure that works for one retrieval task transfers cleanly to another.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined as the aim of developing measures of database retrieval performance that shall be comparable across all information retrieval tasks.

explainer.example: A retrieval researcher seeks one evaluation measure whose scores can be compared meaningfully between two different search tasks.
